title: Q49: Ratio of Areas Equals Square of Altitudes Ratio Proof
question_text: Prove that the ratio of the areas of two similar triangles equals the square of the ratio of their corresponding altitudes.
math_formula: \text{Area}_1 = \frac{1}{2} b_1 h_1, \quad \text{Area}_2 = \frac{1}{2} b_2 h_2 \implies \frac{\text{Area}_1}{\text{Area}_2} = \left(\frac{b_1}{b_2}\right)\left(\frac{h_1}{h_2}\right) = k \cdot k = k^2
optA: Area = 1/2 · base · height; for similar triangles, base ratio b₁/b₂ = k and altitude ratio h₁/h₂ = k; thus Area₁/Area₂ = k · k = k² = (h₁/h₂)².
optB: Area ratio equals altitude ratio k.
optD: Area ratio equals altitude ratio cubed k³.
